Suitable for final year project?

**适合做 final year project，但需要明显缩小范围。** 你现在的构想同时包含数据生成、跨银行字段统一、信用风险评测和 digital twin，全部完成更接近一个研究团队的项目。

最适合 FYP 的核心是：**研究不同输入字段、有限真实数据的情况下，synthetic data 能否支持可信的信用风险模型评测。**

**1. 你找到的痛点成立，但需要更准确地描述**

银行的问题不只是“数据量不足”，也可能是数据不能共享、违约样本少、某些客户群体覆盖不足，以及不同银行的字段和客户分布不同。

因此，不宜直接声称“没有 public benchmark”。已有公开的合成数据评测工具，例如 NIST 的 SDNist，会评估数据效用和隐私。你的研究缺口可以更具体：**如何在字段不同、数据不能直接共享的银行场景下，建立可重复的信用风险评测流程。** [NIST SDNist](https://www.nist.gov/services-resources/software/sdnist-synthetic-data-report-tool)

**2. HSBC 和 BOCHK 的输入不同，不代表完全不能比较**

关键是你想比较什么：

| 比较目标 | 需要控制的条件 |
|---|---|
| 哪个 AI 算法更好？ | 使用相同可用字段、训练数据与测试条件 |
| 哪个完整预测系统更好？ | 可以使用不同字段，但要在相同目标人群、标签定义和测试条件下评估 |
| 哪家银行自己业务上的表现更好？ | 各自测试集的分数不能直接当作公平排名，因为客户与风险分布可能不同 |

例如，两者都预测“未来 12 个月是否违约”，但一家主要面对低风险客户，另一家面对高风险客户，仅比较 accuracy 无法分清差异来自模型还是客户群体。

**所以 benchmark 的核心是共同的评测协议，不一定是所有银行拥有完全相同的字段。**

**3. 不需要覆盖所有银行的所有字段**

可以设计：

- **共同字段**：收入、贷款金额、负债收入比等，统一含义、单位和时间口径。
- **银行特有字段**：作为可选扩展，建立不同的字段配置。
- **统一预测目标**：例如未来 12 个月违约，明确违约定义。
- **统一评测流程**：固定数据划分，评估区分能力、概率校准和不同群体的表现。

你的 generator 接收字段配置、样本量和场景参数，再生成数据。但**用户要求一个新字段，并不意味着系统知道它与违约风险之间的真实关系**；这需要真实数据或明确的建模假设。

**4. “稀疏 seed → 真实 digital twin” 是最大的研究风险**

少量真实数据可以支持初步生成，但不能保证恢复罕见违约、极端经济情景或未出现过的客户群体。生成更多行，也不会自动增加真实信息。

建议把它称为 **configurable synthetic credit-data generator**。只有能够说明它对应什么真实系统、如何校准和持续验证时，再使用 digital twin 这个说法。

还要避免循环验证：**如果模型只在同一个生成器产生的数据上训练和测试，高分可能只说明它学会了生成器的规律。** 应保留生成器从未接触过的真实测试数据；若没有银行数据，就只能验证公开数据或模拟场景下的结论。

**5. 我建议的 FYP 范围**

建议题目：

**Evaluating Synthetic Credit Data for Credit-Risk Benchmarking under Heterogeneous Feature Availability**

核心研究问题：

> 当真实训练数据减少、可用字段不同时，合成数据能否保留信用风险模型在真实测试集上的表现与排名？

可完成的实验设计：

1. 选一个可用的信用风险数据集，先保留独立真实测试集。
2. 用不同字段子集模拟两到三种银行配置，明确这些并非真实 HSBC 或 BOCHK 数据。
3. 比较两种合成方法与真实数据基线。
4. 改变 seed 数据量、字段覆盖率和缺失程度。
5. 比较真实数据训练与合成数据训练后的表现，包括 AUROC、PR-AUC、校准，以及模型排名是否一致。
6. 做一个简单界面，让用户选择字段和样本量并生成数据与评测报告。

**最有价值的成果不是“能生成看起来真实的数据”，而是证明：在什么条件下，这些数据能支持可信评测；在什么条件下不能。**

下周一讨论时，可以这样概括：

> 我想做一个可配置的信用风险合成数据与评测原型，研究有限真实数据和不同字段配置会如何影响 benchmark 的可信度。项目先用公开数据模拟不同银行，重点验证合成数据能否保留真实测试集上的模型表现和排名。
做一下这个的literature review

**文献支持这个方向，但需要调整创新点：合成数据生成、信用风险数据增强、模型排名保持，都已有研究。更值得做的是它们的交叉问题——当银行字段不同、真实 seed 数据有限时，合成 benchmark 的评测结论是否仍然可信。**

**Literature Review：面向异构银行数据的合成信用风险评测**

**研究背景与问题界定**

银行信用风险研究面临的障碍，不仅是数据数量不足，还包括客户信息不能直接共享、违约样本稀少、不同机构的字段和客户分布不一致。因此，synthetic data 的潜在价值包括支持外部研究、补充训练样本，以及建立可共享的模型评测环境。

英国 FCA 的 *Using Synthetic Data in Financial Services*（2024）将数据增强与偏差缓解、系统测试与模型验证、数据共享列为主要应用主题。这份报告为项目的业务动机提供了依据，但它是行业报告，不能替代对生成质量和评测有效性的实验验证。[FCA, 2024](https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/corporate-documents/report-using-synthetic-data-financial-services)

本项目需要区分三个相关但不同的问题：

| 问题 | 需要验证的内容 |
|---|---|
| 合成数据是否逼真？ | 分布、变量关系和业务约束是否合理 |
| 合成数据是否适合训练？ | 在合成数据上训练的模型能否在真实数据上工作 |
| 合成数据是否适合 benchmark？ | 用它比较模型，是否会得出与真实数据一致的结论 |

这一区分决定了文献选择和实验设计：生成质量较高，并不自动意味着它适合公平比较不同银行的 AI。

**1. 表格数据生成：已有成熟方法，但“支持混合字段”不等于“支持任意银行 schema”**

Xu 等人在 NeurIPS 2019 提出的 **CTGAN**，针对表格数据中的连续变量、离散变量和不平衡类别设计条件生成方法。该工作也评估了 TVAE，构成后续表格合成研究常用的基线。[Xu et al., *Modeling Tabular Data using Conditional GAN*, 2019](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2019/hash/254ed7d2de3b23ab10936522dd547b78-Abstract.html)

Kotelnikov 等人的 **TabDDPM** 将扩散模型应用于混合类型表格数据，在论文所测试的数据集上取得了优于多种 GAN/VAE 方法的结果。Zhang 等人的 **TabSyn** 则先把表格编码到连续潜在空间，再使用扩散模型进行生成。这两项工作说明，项目可以采用已有生成器，把主要精力放在评测问题上。[Kotelnikov et al., ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html)；[Zhang et al., ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09656)

不过，这些方法能够处理数值列和类别列，并不意味着一个已训练的生成器能够理解任意新增字段及其风险关系。银行 A 的“月收入”和银行 B 的“年收入”可以通过明确转换进行对齐；“个人收入”和“家庭收入”则涉及不同语义，不能只靠重命名统一。

**对项目的启示：**应把字段含义、单位、时间口径和可用性作为独立设计对象。单纯接入 CTGAN 或 diffusion model，尚未解决跨银行字段问题。

**2. 按需生成：条件生成已有先例，未观测字段仍需要证据**

Borisov 等人的 **GReaT** 将表格记录转化为文本形式，通过自回归语言模型生成数据，并支持以任意已建模字段子集作为条件，采样其他字段。这与“银行提出所需条件，系统返回数据”的构想直接相关。[Borisov et al., *Language Models are Realistic Tabular Data Generators*, ICLR 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06280)

但需要区分三种请求：

- **选择已有字段：**从已经建模的字段集合中输出一个子集。
- **指定已知条件：**例如生成某收入区间或某贷款类别的客户。
- **新增未观测字段：**例如 seed 中从未出现交易流水，现在要求生成流水及其违约关系。

前两种属于已有条件生成技术可以研究的范围。第三种需要额外数据、外部知识或明确假设；字段名称本身无法确定真实联合分布。

一个关键限制是：假设银行 A 只有收入 \(X\) 和违约标签 \(Y\)，银行 B 只有交易行为 \(Z\) 和标签 \(Y\)。即使分别学到了 \(P(X,Y)\) 和 \(P(Z,Y)\)，通常也不能唯一确定 \(P(X,Z,Y)\)。不同的收入—交易行为关系，都可能符合已观察到的数据。

这是本项目的方法论边界：**覆盖所有字段，不等于知道所有字段之间的真实关系。**

**3. 信用风险领域：合成数据训练已有实证，不能直接推出 benchmark 有效**

Muñoz-Cancino 等人的研究与本项目尤其接近。作者比较 CTGAN 和 TVAE，并评估在合成数据上训练的信用评估模型在真实数据上的表现。他们观察到，在该实验设置中，增加属性后，合成数据质量有所下降；合成训练模型的 AUC 和 KS 也低于真实训练基线。[Muñoz-Cancino et al., *Assessment of Creditworthiness Models Privacy-Preserving Training with Synthetic Data*, HAIS 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.01212)

这项研究提供了两个重要依据。第一，信用风险场景中确实可以用真实测试数据检验合成数据的训练效用。第二，“覆盖更多银行字段”可能增加生成难度，字段数量与质量之间需要实验验证。

其适用范围也需要限定：这项工作不能据此证明任意银行都可使用同一生成器，也不能证明跨银行的模型排名会被保留。

因此，FYP 若仅展示“CTGAN 生成信用数据，再训练一个分类器”，与已有工作的重叠会较大。更有价值的延伸是系统改变 **seed 数量、字段覆盖和客户分布**，观察评测结论何时失效。

**4. Benchmark 的直接相关文献：模型排名保持早已被提出**

Jordon、Yoon 和 van der Schaar 在 2018 年的 KDD workshop 论文中提出 **Synthetic Ranking Agreement（SRA）**：如果算法 A 在真实数据上优于算法 B，那么在合成数据上的比较也应尽可能保持这一顺序。它衡量的是算法两两比较的一致程度。[Jordon et al., *Measuring the Quality of Synthetic Data for Use in Competitions*, 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.11345)

这篇论文与本项目的 benchmark 动机最直接相关，也意味着“用合成数据保持模型排名”本身不能作为新的研究贡献。

在实验设计上，应区分：

| 评测方式 | 回答的问题 |
|---|---|
| Train on Synthetic, Test on Real（TSTR） | 合成数据能否支持训练可用模型？ |
| 算法分别在真实与合成数据上训练、测试，再比较排名 | 合成环境能否支持算法选择？ |
| 固定一组已训练模型，分别在真实与合成测试集上评分 | 合成测试集能否替代真实测试集进行评测？ |

后两种也不能混为一谈：一个比较学习算法，另一个比较固定模型。

本项目最适合选择其中一种作为主任务，再把 TSTR 作为辅助指标。除了排名相关性，还应观察“合成 benchmark 选中的最佳模型，在真实数据上损失了多少表现”，避免总体排名看似接近，却选错最优模型。

**5. 跨银行可比性：字段差异和分布差异需要分别处理**

Gardner 等人的 **TableShift** 建立了包含金融等领域的表格分布偏移 benchmark。它表明，模型在原分布上的表现与分布变化后的表现需要分别评估。[Gardner et al., *Benchmarking Distribution Shift in Tabular Data with TableShift*, NeurIPS 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.07577)

Cheng 等人的 **TabFSBench** 则专门研究 feature shifts，评估不同字段变化情境下模型的适用性与性能退化。这是“不同银行拥有不同输入字段”的重要相邻工作；本综述引用其 2025 年 arXiv 版本。[Cheng et al., *TabFSBench: Tabular Benchmark for Feature Shifts in Open Environments*, 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18935)

另外，Yang 等人对横向联邦学习、纵向联邦学习和联邦迁移学习的划分，提供了理解机构间样本与特征重叠关系的框架。不过，联邦学习主要解决协作训练问题，本身不构成统一的公开 benchmark。[Yang et al., *Federated Machine Learning: Concept and Applications*, ACM TIST, 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.04885)

综合这些文献，跨银行差异至少包含四层：

| 差异 | 示例 | 项目需要的处理 |
|---|---|---|
| 字段语义 | 月收入与家庭年收入 | 明确定义与映射规则 |
| 字段可用性 | 一家有交易记录，另一家没有 | 分别定义字段配置 |
| 客户分布 | 不同收入、地区或贷款群体 | 独立评估分布偏移 |
| 标签定义 | 不同违约标准或预测期限 | 统一任务，或分别报告 |

因此，HSBC 与 BOCHK 即使预测“违约”，也不能仅凭各自的 accuracy 排名。相反，在共同任务、共同目标人群和明确字段配置下，可以比较算法或系统表现。这里的两家银行仅作为问题示例，本综述没有证据说明它们实际使用哪些字段。

**6. 合成数据评估：整体相似度不足以证明局部业务可靠性**

**SynthEval** 提供了表格合成数据的效用和隐私评估框架，并注意处理数值与类别属性。它可以减少项目重复实现基础指标的工作，但不能替代针对信用风险任务的评测设计。[Lautrup et al., *SynthEval: A Framework for Detailed Utility and Privacy Evaluation of Tabular Synthetic Data*, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15821)

较新的 **TabQueryBench** 从分析查询角度评估合成表格数据，指出常规统计指标较好的数据，仍可能不能保留局部或尾部查询的结果。本综述引用其 2026 年预印本，不将其视为已确立的普遍结论。[Zhang et al., *TabQueryBench: A Query-Centric Benchmark for Synthetic Tabular Data*, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03926)

对信用风险而言，这提示项目除整体 AUROC 外，还应关注稀少违约样本和特定客户群体。一个合理的评测集合是：

- **统计保真度：**单变量分布、变量关联、业务约束违例。
- **预测效用：**AUROC、PR-AUC、Brier score 或校准表现。
- **benchmark 可靠性：**排名一致性、最佳模型选择一致性、选择错误造成的性能损失。
- **群体与尾部表现：**不同风险或客户分组下的指标。
- **不确定性：**重复数据划分、生成随机种子和置信区间。

这些指标回答不同问题，不宜未经论证就合并成一个总分。

**7. 少量 seed 与隐私：需要实测，不能预设“合成即匿名”**

Stadler 等人的 USENIX Security 2022 论文表明，在其测试的生成方法中，合成数据可能仍暴露信息，隐私与效用之间的权衡也不容易预测。因此，数据经过生成器处理并不构成隐私保证。[Stadler et al., *Synthetic Data – Anonymisation Groundhog Day*, 2022](https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity22/presentation/stadler)

Byun 等人的 **Risk In Context** 专门研究低数据量情境下的表格生成与隐私泄露，包含使用少量示例进行 in-context generation 的方法。该研究报告了 seed 记录泄露风险，与“稀疏真实数据生成 digital twins”的设想直接相关；其 arXiv 页面注明为 KDD 2025 相关 workshop poster。[Byun et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.17066)

对于需要正式隐私约束的扩展，Chen 等人的 **Benchmarking Differentially Private Tabular Data Synthesis** 提供了统一比较差分隐私合成方法的框架，并讨论效用与效率的权衡。[Chen et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14061)

本项目应将“少量 seed 是否足够”作为研究问题，而非前提。生成十万条记录不能弥补 seed 中完全缺失的某类客户证据；即使生成器输出了这类客户，其可信度仍依赖额外假设或外部验证。

**8. Digital twin 的定位**

NIST 关于 digital twin 的讨论强调真实实体的数字表示、状态及状态变化，并涉及与真实对象之间的同步和信任问题。[NIST IR 8356, 2025](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ir/8356/final)

据此，本项目如果只学习静态信用表格并生成记录，使用 **configurable synthetic-data generator** 会更准确。若进一步表示借款人的还款状态随时间演化，并用真实观测持续校准，才更有理由采用 digital twin 的定位。

这个概念区分可以避免项目同时承担静态数据合成、动态信用行为建模和系统同步三个不同任务。

**文献综合：可以成立的 research gap**

本次检索已经找到：

- 通用表格合成方法；
- 合成信用数据的训练效用研究；
- 合成数据上的算法排名一致性；
- 表格分布偏移与字段变化 benchmark；
- 少量数据下的生成与隐私评估。

因此，不宜把研究缺口写成“没有 public benchmark”或“首次利用 synthetic data 比较 AI”。

更有依据的表述是：

> 现有相关研究分别考察表格数据生成、信用风险预测、算法排名保持以及字段与分布变化。本项目将这些问题结合，研究在有限真实 seed 数据和异构字段配置下，合成信用风险 benchmark 能否保留真实数据上的模型选择结论，并识别其可靠性的适用范围。

这是由本次文献综合得到的候选缺口，尚不足以支持“全球首次”的声明。

**建议的 FYP 研究问题与最小实验**

建议题目：

*Reliability of Synthetic Credit-Risk Benchmarks under Limited Seed Data and Heterogeneous Feature Availability*

主研究问题：

> 当 seed 数据量和可用字段发生变化时，合成 benchmark 对信用风险算法的排名，在多大程度上与真实数据评测一致？

建议先固定客户分布，避免一开始同时引入所有变量：

is there an algorithm to generate synthetic data? like diffusion? monte carlo?

**Yes—both diffusion models and Monte Carlo simulation can generate synthetic banking data.** They play different roles: diffusion learns a data distribution, while Monte Carlo means repeatedly sampling from a model you have specified or fitted. They are not mutually exclusive.

For your project, these are the main options:

| Approach | How it generates data | Main consideration |
|---|---|---|
| **Statistical simulation + Monte Carlo** | Specify distributions and relationships, then randomly sample customers and outcomes | Transparent and controllable, but realism depends on your assumptions |
| **Gaussian copula** | Learn each variable’s distribution and their dependence, then sample new records | Useful statistical baseline; may miss complex relationships |
| **GAN — e.g. CTGAN** | Train a generator to produce rows that a discriminator struggles to distinguish from real rows | Designed for mixed numerical and categorical tables |
| **VAE — e.g. TVAE** | Learn a compressed probabilistic representation, sample from it, then decode into rows | Another established neural baseline |
| **Diffusion — e.g. TabDDPM or TabSyn** | Learn to reverse a noise process, then generate new records starting from noise | Can model complex tabular distributions, but needs training data and computation |

Copula sampling is implemented in [SDV’s Copulas library](https://sdv.dev/Copulas/tutorials/03_Multivariate_Distributions.html). CTGAN and TVAE are described in the [CTGAN paper](https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2019/hash/254ed7d2de3b23ab10936522dd547b78-Abstract.html).

**How Monte Carlo would work in your banking example**

You could construct a simplified borrower model:

1. Sample income from a fitted income distribution.
2. Sample loan amount **conditional on income**.
3. Generate repayment history and debt burden using specified relationships.
4. Calculate a default probability from these attributes.
5. Sample a default outcome from that probability.
6. Repeat to generate thousands of borrowers.

The relationships matter: independently sampling realistic-looking income, debt and default values would not necessarily produce realistic customers.

This approach gives you a **controlled synthetic world**. You can change unemployment assumptions or default rates and examine model behaviour. However, success in that world demonstrates performance under your simulation assumptions; real-data validation is still needed.

**How diffusion would work**

During training, the model progressively corrupts real borrower records and learns to reverse that corruption. During generation, it starts from noise and produces new records.

**TabDDPM** adapts diffusion to numerical and categorical columns. **TabSyn** first encodes mixed-type rows into a continuous latent space, then performs diffusion there. These are directly relevant to credit-risk tables. [TabDDPM, ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html); [TabSyn, ICLR 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09656)

The target is to learn a joint distribution such as:

\[
P(\text{income},\text{debt},\text{repayment history},\text{default})
\]

That is what allows generated fields and labels to have meaningful relationships. **Diffusion cannot establish the real relationship of a field that never appears in its training evidence.**

**For your FYP, I would compare three generators: Gaussian copula, CTGAN and TabDDPM.** Add a hand-designed Monte Carlo simulator if you want controlled experiments where the true generating process is known.

Then ask:

> **Which generation method best preserves credit-risk model rankings as seed data becomes smaller and available fields change?**

That connects the generation algorithm to your original benchmark problem—and gives you a research contribution beyond simply generating a dataset.

what is TabDDPM

**TabDDPM (Tabular Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model)** is an AI model that generates synthetic table rows containing numerical and categorical fields.

It works in two stages:

1. **Training:** Gradually corrupt real records with noise and teach the model to reverse that process.
2. **Generation:** Start with random noise and progressively turn it into new synthetic records.

For your project, it could learn from real credit records and generate new combinations of credit limits, repayment histories, bill amounts and default labels.

**Its main limitation:** It needs representative training data. It cannot reliably recover customer groups or relationships missing from the seed data.

Reference: [TabDDPM — ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html).
can we generate a dataset with probability distributions with TabDDPM? for example, occupations in hk have a distribution, maybe students are more than doctors

**Yes. TabDDPM can learn occupation frequencies from training data, and you can also design generation to target a specified distribution.**

There are two cases:

- **Learn the distribution:** If your seed data contains 30% students and 5% doctors, TabDDPM aims to reproduce that pattern approximately. Exact proportions are not guaranteed.
- **Specify the distribution:** If you want exactly 3,000 students and 500 doctors in 10,000 records, use **conditional generation with quotas**. This requires configuring or adapting the model to condition on occupation; arbitrary-column conditioning is not automatically available in every TabDDPM implementation.

The important part is generating the **other fields conditional on occupation**:

\[
P(\text{occupation},\text{other fields})
=
P(\text{occupation})\,P(\text{other fields}\mid\text{occupation})
\]

For example, first select “student” according to your target proportions, then generate income, debt and repayment history appropriate to students. Simply changing occupation labels afterward could create inconsistent records.

Also, define whose distribution you want: **Hong Kong residents, loan applicants, or a bank’s customers** can have different occupation proportions. “Student” may need a broader employment-status category rather than occupation.

Your idea is feasible: **use external statistics to set category proportions, and real seed data to learn relationships between fields.**
how do we distinguish the “generation” with “classification”?

They serve different purposes:

- **Generation** learns the overall data distribution  
  \[
  P(X,Y)
  \]
  and creates new synthetic records—for example, occupation, income, repayment history, and default status.

- **Classification** learns the relationship  
  \[
  P(Y\mid X)
  \]
  and predicts a label for an existing record—for example, whether a customer will default based on their features.

In your project:

1. **TabDDPM generates** synthetic customer records.
2. A classifier such as logistic regression or XGBoost is **trained and evaluated** on those records.
3. Its results are compared with performance on real data to judge whether the synthetic dataset is useful.

Example:

- Generator output: `Student, HK$8,000 income, low debt, no default`
- Classifier input: `Student, HK$8,000 income, low debt`
- Classifier output: `12% probability of default`

The generator creates the benchmark data; the classifier is the model being benchmarked.

Yes. Learning the full joint distribution \(P(X,Y)\) can require substantial data, especially when there are many fields, rare categories, or complex dependencies. TabDDPM may overfit or generate unreliable combinations when the initial dataset is small.

For a small seed dataset, use a more constrained strategy:

- Start with fewer, important fields.
- Use simple models such as Gaussian copulas or Bayesian networks as baselines.
- Use external aggregate statistics—for example, Hong Kong occupation and age distributions—to set marginal distributions.
- Learn only the relationships supported by the seed data, such as \(P(\text{income}\mid\text{occupation})\).
- Encode known business constraints, such as non-negative income and loan amount.
- Treat rare groups carefully; generating extra rows does not create information missing from the seed.
- Validate using held-out real records and check whether generated records merely copy seed rows.

A practical hybrid model would be:

\[
P(X,Y)
=
P_{\text{external}}(\text{age, occupation})
\times
P_{\text{seed}}(\text{income, debt, repayment}\mid\text{age, occupation})
\times
P_{\text{seed}}(\text{default}\mid X)
\]

For the FYP, this limitation can become the research question:

> How does seed-data size affect the realism and benchmarking reliability of synthetic credit-risk data?

You could train generators using 100, 500, 1,000, and 5,000 seed records, then measure when statistical fidelity, classifier performance, and model-ranking agreement begin to fail. For very small samples, I would begin with Monte Carlo or copula methods and treat TabDDPM as a comparison method rather than the assumed best solution.
[TabDDPM — ICML 2023](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a.html). Tell me more about this paper, and given our concerns just mentioned, do you think it is a good approach?

**TabDDPM is worth testing, but I would treat it as a candidate generator—not assume it solves our small-data and cross-bank problems.** Reading the paper also reveals an important detail about how it generates labels.

**What the paper proposes**

TabDDPM combines two diffusion processes:

- **Numerical fields**, such as income: Gaussian noise is added during training.
- **Categorical fields**, such as occupation: categories are progressively corrupted using multinomial diffusion.
- A shared neural network learns to reverse both processes, allowing it to capture relationships between fields.

For classification datasets, it learns **\(P(X\mid Y)\)**: customer features conditional on a supplied label. To create complete records, select a label, then generate its features. Together with a label distribution \(P(Y)\), this defines \(P(X,Y)\). [Paper, Section 4](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a/kotelnikov23a.pdf)

For example, we could select “default” and then generate a borrower profile consistent with that outcome. The generator is still distinct from a classifier, which predicts default from a profile.

**What its experiments demonstrate**

The authors evaluate statistical similarity and **training on synthetic data, testing on real data**. TabDDPM generally outperforms their GAN/VAE alternatives, although simple SMOTE interpolation is competitive on predictive utility.

They include small datasets: Diabetes has **491 training records**. However, their Default dataset has **19,200 training records**. This is not a systematic experiment on shrinking banking seed data. The authors also acknowledge unresolved privacy limitations. [Paper, Sections 5 and limitations](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a/kotelnikov23a.pdf)

**How it fits our concerns**

| Our concern | My assessment |
|---|---|
| Only a small initial dataset | Possible to experiment with, but success depends on field complexity and coverage of rare groups. There is no universal minimum sample size. |
| Specify HK occupation proportions | We need an additional mechanism to enforce those proportions. The paper’s classification setup conditions on the target label; it does not directly provide arbitrary occupation-and-default controls. |
| Different fields across banks | We still need field definitions and mappings. A generator trained on one schema cannot establish relationships for unseen fields. |
| Build a trustworthy benchmark | Good synthetic training utility does not establish that model rankings on a synthetic benchmark match rankings on real data. We must test that separately. |

For the occupation example, we could generate complete records and **select records to meet occupation quotas**. This preserves each selected record’s internal relationships, but depends on the generator producing enough credible examples of every group. More advanced occupation-conditioned generation would require adaptation.

Also, knowing that students are more common than doctors tells us \(P(\text{occupation})\). It does **not** tell us their income, debt, or default relationships. External statistics help constrain generation, while seed data or explicit assumptions must supply those relationships.

**My recommendation at this stage:** compare a simple statistical generator with TabDDPM using progressively smaller seeds. Check field distributions, rare-group coverage, predictive performance on untouched real records, and model-ranking agreement.

That would let us answer a useful question: **When does diffusion provide enough additional value to justify its complexity—and when is the seed data too limited for either approach to be reliable?**

margina distribution and joint distribution conform to what relationship in integral?

The **marginal distribution is obtained by integrating out the other variables from the joint distribution**.

For continuous variables \(X\) and \(Y\), with joint probability density \(f_{X,Y}(x,y)\):

\[
\boxed{f_X(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f_{X,Y}(x,y)\,dy}
\]

Similarly,

\[
f_Y(y)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f_{X,Y}(x,y)\,dx.
\]

For categorical variables, replace the integral with a sum. For example:

\[
P(\text{district}=d)
=
\sum_o P(\text{district}=d,\text{occupation}=o).
\]

Intuitively: to find how many people live in district \(d\), add up everyone there across all occupations.

The reverse direction is important for our project: **knowing the marginals does not uniquely determine the joint distribution.** Knowing district proportions and occupation proportions does not tell us which occupations live in which districts.

Only if we assume independence can we write:

\[
f_{X,Y}(x,y)=f_X(x)f_Y(y).
\]

More generally,

\[
f_{X,Y}(x,y)=f_X(x)f_{Y\mid X}(y\mid x).
\]

So external statistics can provide the marginals, while the seed data—or explicit assumptions—must supply the dependence between variables.
mathematically if we have n variables can we derive joint distribution from a set of marginal distributions?

**Generally, no.** Even if you know the marginal distribution of every variable, you cannot uniquely recover their joint distribution. The marginals do not specify how the variables depend on each other.

For \(n\) continuous variables, each marginal satisfies:

\[
f_i(x_i)
=
\int_{\mathbb R^{n-1}}
f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\prod_{j\ne i}dx_j.
\]

Many different joint densities \(f\) satisfy exactly the same marginal constraints.

For a simple example, suppose \(X,Y\in\{0,1\}\), and both are equally likely to be 0 or 1:

| Joint probability | Independent | Always equal | Always opposite |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| \(P(0,0)\) | 0.25 | 0.50 | 0 |
| \(P(0,1)\) | 0.25 | 0 | 0.50 |
| \(P(1,0)\) | 0.25 | 0 | 0.50 |
| \(P(1,1)\) | 0.25 | 0.50 | 0 |

All three have **identical marginals**, but completely different relationships.

You can determine the joint if you add sufficient information:

- **Assume mutual independence:**
  \[
  f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}f_i(x_i).
  \]
  This constructs one possible joint; the marginals alone do not justify the assumption.

- **Know the required conditional distributions:**
  \[
  f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
  =
  f_1(x_1)\prod_{i=2}^{n}f(x_i\mid x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1}).
  \]
  This is the chain rule and requires no independence assumption.

Even knowing **all pairwise joint distributions** generally does not determine the full joint when \(n\geq3\), because higher-order relationships can remain unknown.

For your project, population statistics constrain the possible synthetic datasets. **The 100 customer records help estimate which dependence structure is plausible—but they may not identify it reliably.**

Please walk me through what is TabDDPM mathematically and how to test the model

**TabDDPM learns how to turn random noise into a realistic table row.** For your project, that means learning to generate income, loan amount, institution, approval outcome, and the other fields together.

Let’s connect the mathematics to your HMDA implementation.

**1. What distribution are we learning?**

Represent one mortgage record as

\[
x=(u,c)
\]

where:

- \(u\) contains numerical fields, such as income and loan amount.
- \(c\) contains categorical fields, such as institution and approval outcome.

Our objective is:

\[
p_\theta(u,c)\approx p_{\text{real}}(u,c)
\]

Here, \(\theta\) denotes the neural network’s learned parameters.

This is a **joint distribution**. Matching income and loan-amount distributions separately is insufficient: the model must also learn which incomes tend to occur with which loan amounts.

In our implementation, approval is another generated field:

\[
p_\theta(\text{income},\text{loan amount},\text{bank},\text{approval},\ldots)
\]

**2. How numerical diffusion works**

First, our preprocessing transforms numerical values into approximately normal marginal distributions. Conceptually:

\[
u_j=\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\widehat F_j(x_j)\right)
\]

where \(\widehat F_j\) is the training-data empirical CDF and \(\Phi^{-1}\) is the standard normal quantile function. This changes each field’s scale; it does not make the fields independent.

The forward diffusion process adds Gaussian noise:

\[
u_t=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,u_0+
\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,\epsilon,
\qquad \epsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,I)
\]

with

\[
\alpha_t=1-\beta_t,\qquad
\bar\alpha_t=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\alpha_s.
\]

The schedule \(\beta_t\) controls corruption. Early \(t\) retains much of the record; late \(t\) approaches noise. TabDDPM combines this Gaussian process with categorical diffusion. [Paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a/kotelnikov23a.pdf)

For intuition, when \(\bar\alpha_t=0.8\),

\[
u_t=\sqrt{0.8}\,u_0+\sqrt{0.2}\,\epsilon.
\]

This equation applies to **transformed values**, not directly to dollars.

**3. How categorical diffusion works**

For a field with \(K\) categories:

\[
q(c_t=k\mid c_{t-1}=j)
=
\alpha_t\,\mathbf1[k=j]+\frac{1-\alpha_t}{K}.
\]

The category is retained with probability \(\alpha_t\); otherwise a category is drawn uniformly, possibly the same one. Repeated corruption approaches a uniform distribution.

The network receives the **whole corrupted row and timestep**, and predicts numerical noise plus categorical reconstruction probabilities. Numerical training minimizes

\[
\mathcal L_{\text{num}}
=
\mathbb E\!\left[
\frac{1}{d_{\text{num}}}
\left\|
\epsilon-\epsilon_\theta(u_t,c_t,t)
\right\|^2
\right].
\]

Categorical training uses reverse-transition KL terms, schematically:

\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(
q(c_{t-1}\mid c_t,c_0)
\,\Vert\,
p_\theta(c_{t-1}\mid u_t,c_t)
\right),
\]

with a reconstruction term at the final denoising step. Our code combines numerical loss with categorical variational loss averaged across categorical fields. [Official implementation](https://github.com/yandex-research/tab-ddpm/blob/main/tab_ddpm/gaussian_multinomial_diffsuion.py)

The crucial point is the network’s shared input. To reconstruct a corrupted loan amount, it can use information from income, institution, property value, and other fields.

**4. What happens during training and generation?**

Each training iteration:

1. Selects real training rows.
2. Samples a noise timestep for each row.
3. Corrupts the rows at those timesteps.
4. Calculates reconstruction losses.
5. Updates the network parameters.

We can construct \(u_t\) directly using the formula above. Training does not need to run all 1,000 corruption steps sequentially for every row.

Generation runs in reverse:

\[
\underbrace{x_T}_{\text{random noise}}
\longrightarrow x_{T-1}
\longrightarrow\cdots
\longrightarrow
\underbrace{x_0}_{\text{synthetic record}}.
\]

Numerical coordinates start Gaussian; categorical coordinates start uniform. Learned reverse transitions produce a record, which is decoded into original units and category labels. [Paper](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/kotelnikov23a/kotelnikov23a.pdf)

There is **no corresponding “correct real row”** for a synthetic row. We therefore test distributions and relationships, rather than row-by-row prediction error.

**5. How should we test your model?**

I recommend evaluating four questions.

| Question | Example in HMDA | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Are individual fields realistic? | Income distribution; bank proportions | KS, Wasserstein distance, categorical total variation |
| Are relationships realistic? | Loan amount versus income; approval within each bank | Correlations and conditional distributions |
| Are rare cases represented? | Very high property values; negative income | Tail frequencies, quantiles, subgroup counts |
| Is it copying records? | Synthetic rows identical or very close to training rows | Exact matches and nearest-neighbour analysis |

Your existing script implements the first three **partially**, plus exact-match and duplicate checks. Nearest-neighbour analysis and broader conditional checks are not implemented yet.

For numerical distributions, the KS distance is

\[
D_{\text{KS}}
=
\sup_z
\left|\widehat F_{\text{real}}(z)-\widehat F_{\text{synthetic}}(z)\right|.
\]

It measures the largest gap between the two empirical CDFs. Smaller is better.

For categories, total variation is

\[
D_{\text{TV}}
=
\frac12\sum_k
\left|\widehat p_{\text{real}}(k)-\widehat p_{\text{synthetic}}(k)\right|.
\]

For a binary category, proportions of 75% versus 70% give \(D_{\text{TV}}=0.05\).

Neither metric tests the full joint distribution. A generator could independently sample every column and get excellent marginal scores while producing unrealistic combinations.

For your project, I would therefore also compare quantities such as

\[
P(\text{approved}\mid \text{bank}=b,\text{income group}=g)
\]

and

\[
P(\text{loan amount}>L\mid \text{income group}=g).
\]

Use sufficiently populated groups and report their sample counts.

**6. How do we test extreme cases fairly?**

Choose thresholds using training data only. For example:

\[
\tau=Q_{0.99}(\text{training income}).
\]

Then compare

\[
\widehat P_{\text{test}}(\text{income}>\tau)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat P_{\text{synthetic}}(\text{income}>\tau).
\]

Also examine the other fields within that tail: high incomes paired with implausible loan amounts would still indicate a failure.

Your code now reports these tail frequencies and extreme quantiles. Two cautions matter:

- A maximum depends strongly on sample size; compare similarly sized datasets or repeated samples.
- The current inverse quantile transform is bounded by training values. A real test value beyond that range reveals a genuine limitation of this version.

Preserving extreme training observations is necessary, but does not guarantee that the generator reproduces their frequency or relationships.

这份 **2024 年 Delaware HMDA CSV 一共有 99 个字段**。下面按文件中的实际顺序逐一解释。字段含义参照 [HMDA 官方数据字典](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields)。

先记住三个区别：

- **一行是一笔贷款或贷款申请**，不一定是一个独立的人。
- 很多数字是**类别编码**，例如 `loan_type=2`，不能当作连续数值。
- 公开数据经过隐私处理：没有具体信用分和完整地址，年龄按区间发布，贷款金额和房产价值按区间中点发布。[公开数据处理说明](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/HMDA_Disclosure_FPG_--_Final_12.21.2018_for_website_with_date.pdf)

**1–12：年份、机构、地理位置和汇总分类**

| # | 字段 | 中文解释 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `activity_year` | 数据所属年份；我们的文件是 2024 年。 |
| 2 | `lei` | 报送金融机构的法人识别码，用于区分银行、按揭公司等机构；不是客户编号。 |
| 3 | `derived_msa-md` | 房产所在的大都市统计区／都市分区代码，表示较大的经济与地理区域。 |
| 4 | `state_code` | 房产所在州的缩写，例如 `DE` 是 Delaware。 |
| 5 | `county_code` | 房产所在县的 FIPS 编码，包含州和县的识别信息。 |
| 6 | `census_tract` | 房产所在人口普查小区的编号，比县更细；不是街道地址。 |
| 7 | `conforming_loan_limit` | 贷款金额是否符合政府支持企业的 conforming loan 金额上限。`C` 符合；`NC` 不符合；也有无法确定、不适用。 |
| 8 | `derived_loan_product_type` | 将贷款类型与抵押权顺位合并后的产品分类，例如“普通贷款＋第一顺位抵押”。 |
| 9 | `derived_dwelling_category` | 将建筑方式和住房单元数合并后的住宅分类，例如“现场建造的 1–4 单元住宅”。 |
| 10 | `derived_ethnicity` | 综合申请人与共同申请人信息得到的族裔分类；主要涉及是否为 Hispanic/Latino，也可能为 Joint。 |
| 11 | `derived_race` | 综合申请人与共同申请人信息得到的种族分类；不是只看主申请人的种族。 |
| 12 | `derived_sex` | 综合申请人与共同申请人信息得到的性别分类，例如 Male、Female、Joint。 |

这些 `derived_*` 字段是由其他字段计算出来的。将来生成全部字段时，需要保证它们与原始字段一致。

**13–21：申请结果、贷款类型和用途**

| # | 字段 | 中文解释 |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | `action_taken` | 申请或贷款的处理结果。我们的文件只包含：`1` 已发放贷款；`2` 已批准但申请人未接受；`3` 拒绝。完整 HMDA 还包括撤回、资料不完整等情况。 |
| 14 | `purchaser_type` | 如果机构将贷款卖出，购买方属于什么类型，例如 Fannie Mae、Freddie Mac、银行等。**不是购房人的类型。** |
| 15 | `preapproval` | 是否申请了购房贷款预批准：`1` 申请过；`2` 未申请。不是是否获得最终批准。 |
| 16 | `loan_type` | 贷款类别：`1` 普通贷款；`2` FHA 保险贷款；`3` VA 担保贷款；`4` RHS/FSA 担保贷款。 |
| 17 | `loan_purpose` | 贷款用途：`1` 购房；`2` 房屋改善；`31` 再融资；`32` 套现再融资；`4` 其他；`5` 不适用。 |
| 18 | `lien_status` | 抵押权顺位：`1` 第一顺位；`2` 次级顺位。影响抵押物处置时的受偿顺序。 |
| 19 | `reverse_mortgage` | 是否为反向抵押贷款，即以房产权益取得资金的贷款安排。 |
| 20 | `open-end_line_of_credit` | 是否为可循环使用的信贷额度，例如房屋净值信用额度；不是信用评分。 |
| 21 | `business_or_commercial_purpose` | 贷款是否主要用于商业或经营目的。 |

**22–38：金额、利率、费用和还款条款**

| # | 字段 | 中文解释 |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | `loan_amount` | 已发放或申请的贷款金额，单位为**美元**。公开值采用所在 10,000 美元区间的中点，不是原始精确金额。 |
| 23 | `loan_to_value_ratio` | 房产担保的总债务与房产估值之比，单位为百分比；对应官方定义中的 **combined LTV**，可能包含其他抵押债务。 |
| 24 | `interest_rate` | 贷款利率，按百分数表示，例如 `6.5` 表示 6.5%。 |
| 25 | `rate_spread` | 贷款 APR 与可比贷款平均最优惠报价利率 APOR 的差，通常按百分点表示；不是利率本身。 |
| 26 | `hoepa_status` | 是否属于 HOEPA 定义的高成本抵押贷款：`1` 是；`2` 否；`3` 不适用。 |
| 27 | `total_loan_costs` | 按规定口径报告的贷款总费用，单位美元；不是整个贷款期限内的本金加利息。 |
| 28 | `total_points_and_fees` | 按相应规则计算的 points 和费用总额，单位美元；与上一字段口径不同，不能直接相加。 |
| 29 | `origination_charges` | 为办理、发放贷款收取的相关费用，单位美元，例如贷款办理费。 |

| 31 | `lender_credits` | 贷款机构提供、用于抵扣成交费用的金额，单位美元；**不是借款人的信用额度或信用分。** |
| 32 | `loan_term` | 贷款期限，单位**月**。例如 `360` 表示 30 年。 |
| 33 | `prepayment_penalty_term` | 提前还款罚金条款适用的期限，单位月；不是罚金金额。 |
| 34 | `intro_rate_period` | 从贷款成交／开户到利率首次可能调整之间的月数，即初始利率保持期。 |
| 35 | `negative_amortization` | 是否允许负摊销：还款不足以覆盖利息，未付利息计入余额，使欠款可能增加。 |

| 37 | `balloon_payment` | 是否包含某次需要支付大额尾款的安排。 |
| 38 | `other_nonamortizing_features` | 是否包含其他不能按常规还款逐步完全偿清本金的条款。 |

这里尤其要注意：**不能用公开的 `loan_amount / property_value` 强行重算并要求等于 `loan_to_value_ratio`**，因为公开金额经过分箱，而且该比例可能包含多笔抵押债务。[字段定义](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields#combined_loan_to_value_ratio)

aus是什么

**AUS = Automated Underwriting System，自动承保／贷款审批系统。** 可以理解为银行用来辅助审核房贷申请的软件。

它会根据收入、债务、信用记录、贷款金额、房产价值等信息，评估申请是否满足相关贷款要求，并给出审核建议。**它不一定使用 AI，也可能主要依靠规则和统计模型；最终决定仍由贷款机构作出。**

在你的 HMDA 数据里：

- `aus-1` 到 `aus-5`：记录这笔申请使用过哪些 AUS，最多记录五个。
- 例如 `1` 表示 **Desktop Underwriter（DU）**；`2` 表示 **Loan Prospector / Loan Product Advisor**。
- 这些数字是**系统名称的编码**，不是评分、风险等级或审批结果。

例如一行数据的 `aus-1 = 1`，意思是“这笔申请使用了 DU 系统”，不能理解为“信用等级为 1”。实际贷款处理结果要看 `action_taken`。
有什么denial reason

HMDA 的拒贷原因记录在 `denial_reason-1` 到 `denial_reason-4`，一笔申请最多报告 **4 个主要原因**：

| 编码 | 拒贷原因 | 通俗解释 |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | 负债收入比（DTI） | 相对于收入，每月需要偿还的债务过多。 |
| **2** | 就业历史 | 就业经历或稳定性未满足贷款要求。 |
| **3** | 信用历史 | 信用记录未满足要求，例如存在逾期记录。 |
| **4** | 抵押物 | 房产价值或抵押物条件未满足要求。 |
| **5** | 现金不足 | 缺少支付首付、成交费用等所需的资金。 |
| **6** | 信息无法核实 | 无法核实申请人提供的收入、工作等信息。 |
| **7** | 申请资料不完整 | 缺少审批所需的资料。 |
| **8** | 抵押贷款保险被拒 | 所需的房贷保险申请未获批准。 |
| **9** | 其他 | 不属于上述类别的原因。 |
| **10** | 不适用 | 表示该拒贷原因字段不适用，不是一种拒贷原因。 |

例如，`denial_reason-1 = 1`、`denial_reason-2 = 3`，表示报告的原因包括**负债收入比和信用历史**。后缀 `-1`、`-2` 是记录位置，不应理解为严重程度排名。

这些字段给出原因类别，**不会提供具体信用分，也不会说明“收入还差多少才能通过”**。[HMDA 官方定义](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields#denial_reason-1)
啥是seed sd

这里的 **seed SD** 是指：

- **seed**：随机种子（random seed），例如 `42`、`43`、`44`。
- **SD**：standard deviation，标准差。

在我们的评估中，会用不同的随机种子重复实验，例如：

```text
seed = 42
seed = 43
seed = 44
```

每次会随机抽取不同的真实数据和合成数据子集，并重新训练检测器。假设得到三个 AUC：

```text
0.75, 0.76, 0.74
```

那么：

- Mean AUC ≈ `0.75`
- Seed SD ≈ `0.01`

它表达的是：**换一个随机抽样方式后，评估结果会不会变化很大。**

解释方式：

- **Mean AUC**：平均检测效果。
- **Seed SD 小**：结果比较稳定。
- **Seed SD 大**：结果对抽样方式敏感，应该增加重复次数或样本量。

需要注意，seed SD 不是正式的置信区间，也不是模型本身的标准差。它只是反映不同随机种子下的实验波动。

is there a way to improve CTGAN?

Yes. **Your CTGAN is a baseline using mostly default settings, so there are several reasonable improvements to test.** But we should target the weaknesses your results reveal.

For SVM, training on CTGAN data reduced AUC from **0.860 to 0.750** and denied recall from **53.4% to 22.4%**. This suggests problems beyond simply generating slightly too many approved applications. The precise cause still needs investigation.

I would improve it in this order:

| Priority | Change | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compare real and synthetic data **separately for approved and denied applications** | Find which income, debt-ratio, loan-size, or bank relationships CTGAN fails to preserve. |
| 2 | Check missing-value patterns and clipping diagnostics | Artificial missingness or values accumulating at numerical boundaries can distort what classifiers learn. |
| 3 | Compare **300, 600, and 1,000 epochs** | Test whether longer training helps. More epochs are not guaranteed to improve a GAN. |
| 4 | Test numerical transformations that preserve extremes | A reversible signed-log transform can reduce scale differences without deleting high values or negative income. |
| 5 | Tune learning rates, network size, and discriminator updates | The default configuration may not suit this dataset. |

CTGAN already includes mechanisms for mixed numerical distributions and imbalanced categories; simply “turning on conditional generation” is not a missing basic feature. Its implementation exposes these training settings. [CTGAN paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00503), [official implementation](https://github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN/blob/main/ctgan/synthesizers/ctgan.py)

There are two more targeted experiments worth considering.

**Generate approved and denied records conditionally.** Conceptually:

\[
P(X,Y)=P(Y)\,P(X\mid Y)
\]

Here, \(Y\) is approval and \(X\) contains the other fields. We can request each outcome and combine the records using the **real training-set proportions**. We must verify that generated labels satisfy the requested condition. This controls the outcome mix, but it will not automatically repair incorrect relationships within each group.

**Investigate the 507-category bank field.** Some banks have very few records, making their individual patterns difficult to learn. A controlled experiment without `lei`—removing it consistently from both real and synthetic classifier inputs—would show whether institution modelling is a major difficulty. That is a diagnostic experiment, not a reason to silently remove banks from the final benchmark.

Before selecting improvements, we should create a validation split inside the training data and refit candidate generators on that smaller training portion. what is balanced accuracy

Balanced accuracy is the average of the recall for each class.

For binary classification:

\[
\text{Balanced Accuracy}
=
\frac{\text{Recall}_{\text{approved}}+\text{Recall}_{\text{denied}}}{2}
\]

where:

\[
\text{Recall}_{\text{approved}}
=
\frac{\text{correctly approved}}{\text{all actually approved}}
\]

\[
\text{Recall}_{\text{denied}}
=
\frac{\text{correctly denied}}{\text{all actually denied}}
\]

It gives both classes equal importance, even when one class is much more common.

In your HMDA data, approved applications are much more common than denied applications. A model that always predicts “approved” could achieve high ordinary accuracy, but it would have zero ability to recognize denied applications. Balanced accuracy exposes this problem.

For example, if:

- approved recall = 90%
- denied recall = 50%

then:

\[
\text{Balanced Accuracy}=\frac{90\%+50\%}{2}=70\%
\]

So balanced accuracy is more informative than ordinary accuracy for your imbalanced approval dataset.

3. **按审批结果逐组对照统计数据。** 比如，合成数据的**整体**贷款金额可能看着挺准，但其中**拒贷组**的贷款金额可能普遍偏小。现在训练会单独比较每组的数字分布特征和类别比例，让这种偏差也进入训练损失。

是做了一个upsampling吗

对，**训练时做了过采样（upsampling）**。每个 batch 都从 `1`（已放款）、`2`（获批但未接受）、`3`（拒贷）各抽约 85 条，**有放回抽样**。所以样本少的组，同一条真实记录更容易被重复抽到，生成器也就有更多机会学习这组的特征。

这只改变了**训练时看到各组的频率**。生成最终那 10,000 条合成数据时，决策标签仍按真实训练集的比例抽取，所以输出里三组并不是各占三分之一。
如何“多练少见的结果”

具体做法是**每次组 batch 时，按结果分别抽样**。

原来是把所有真实申请混在一起随机抽。已放款的记录多，自然就经常被抽到。现在每个 batch 都从三组各抽 **85 条**：85 条已放款、85 条获批但未接受、85 条拒贷。抽样是**有放回的**，所以较小的组里，同一条真实记录可能被反复抽到。

接着，生成器也按这批标签生成 **85 条对应每种结果的合成申请**。判别器把真实和合成申请放在同一结果下比较，训练还会逐组比较统计特征。这样，拒贷组即使在原始数据里占比较低，也会在**每一次参数更新**中给生成器提供反馈。这就是“多练”：提高少见结果在训练中的出现频率。
如何“让discriminator反馈更稳定”

我们用的是**谱归一化（spectral normalization）**。它限制判别器每一层能把输入变化放大多少。
